input.prompt: An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted cotton textile, a long horizontal border band, photographed flat and straight-on so the painted cloth fills the entire frame edge to edge with no margin. Subject: the sea at Visakhapatnam. Rows of stylised rolling waves drawn in the traditional kalamkari water convention fill the whole band: stacked scalloped indigo-blue wave bands ending in spiral curls, each crest edged with ecru and a row of tiny black dots, the troughs filled with fine parallel kalam lines and dotted cross-hatching, so no area of colour is left plain. Swimming among the waves: several patterned fish with scale fills and one crab. Riding the waves are two traditional wooden fishing catamarans (teppa), each a few lashed logs drawn in ecru and madder red with dotted and striped fills (not brown, no wood-grain realism), with a single triangular sail filled with madder, indigo and yellow stripes, dots and petal patterns, no people aboard. Along the top edge runs a line of rounded green hills with dotted fills, and a round myrobalan-yellow sun with petal-shaped rays sits above the hills, set against a deep madder-red sky. A thin band of dots runs along the very top edge and another along the very bottom edge. The scene continues off both the left and right ends with no border, no frame and no edge decoration at the left or right. Style: match the reference image exactly in palette, line quality, fill patterns and cotton texture. Freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red (brick red), indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; dense hand-drawn fill patterns of dots, cross-hatching, scales and tiny petals; visible hand-woven cotton weave and slight dye bleed at the edges of colour areas. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No text, no letters, no writing, no numbers, no signature, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames. The black outlines must look hand-drawn with a bamboo kalam: slightly wobbly, varying in thickness, never mechanically uniform; dye colours slightly bleed past the outlines like a real hand-painted cloth, not a vector illustration.
